questions.question: Which of the following ministries introduced the Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Amendment Bill, 2024, in the parliament?

options.text: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Amendment Bill, 2024, was introduced by the **Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas** in the Parliament.
 
• This amendment aims to modernize the existing Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Act, 1948, **to align with current industry practices and challenges**.
 
• The Bill seeks to enhance **efficiency in oilfield operations** and ensure better regulation of exploration and production activities.
 
• It also aims to facilitate **foreign and domestic investment** in India's oil and gas sector while ensuring environmental safeguards.
 
• The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas is responsible for the development and regulation of **petroleum, natural gas, and related industries** in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Act, 1948**

 
 
• The original Act was enacted to regulate the exploration and development of oilfields in India.
 
• It provides the framework for granting licenses and leases for petroleum and natural gas exploration.
 
• The Act ensures that oilfield operations are conducted in a manner that safeguards **national interests and environmental standards**.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas**
 
 
• The Ministry oversees the exploration, production, distribution, and pricing of petroleum and natural gas in India.
 
• It also regulates the downstream sector, including refining and marketing of petroleum products.
 
• The Ministry plays a key role in ensuring India’s **energy security** and reducing dependency on imports.
 
 
 
• **India's Oil and Gas Sector**
 
 
• India is the third-largest consumer of crude oil and natural gas globally.
 
• The government has launched initiatives like the Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy (HELP) to boost exploration activities.
 
• The sector contributes significantly to India’s GDP and supports industrial growth.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Safeguards in Oilfield Operations**
 
 
• Regulations mandate the use of advanced technology to minimize environmental impact.
 
• Operators are required to adhere to stringent norms for waste management, air quality, and water resource protection.
 
• Environmental Impact Assessments (EIA) are mandatory for new oilfield projects.

questions.question: In which of the following states did the Indian classical dance Bharatanatyam originate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bharatanatyam** is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, originating in Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is deeply rooted in **Natya Shastra**, the ancient Sanskrit text on performing arts attributed to Bharata.
 
• The dance form was traditionally performed in temples as an offering to the deities, combining **expressive gestures (Mudras)**, rhythmic movements, and storytelling.
 
• Bharatanatyam is characterized by its **graceful movements, intricate footwork, and evocative facial expressions**.
 
• The dance style is performed to Carnatic music and is often used to narrate stories from **Hindu mythology**, particularly focusing on themes of devotion (Bhakti).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Natya Shastra:**

 
 
• An ancient treatise written by Bharata that serves as the foundational text for Indian classical dance and drama.
 
• It outlines the principles of aesthetics, gestures, expressions, and stagecraft integral to performing arts.
 
 
 
• **Components of Bharatanatyam:**
 
 
• **Nritta:** Pure dance movements focusing on rhythm and technique.
 
• **Nritya:** Expressive dance using gestures and facial expressions to convey emotions.
 
• **Natya:** The dramatic aspect involving storytelling and enactment.
 
 
 
• **Costume and Makeup:**
 
 
• Dancers wear traditional silk sarees with intricate borders and jewelry.
 
• Makeup emphasizes facial expressions and eye movements, essential for conveying emotions.
 
 
 
• **Famous Bharatanatyam Practitioners:**
 
 
• Rukmini Devi Arundale: A pioneer who redefined Bharatanatyam as a respected art form.
 
• Padma Subrahmanyam: Known for her innovative approach to Bharatanatyam.

questions.question: When natural resources are unlimited, the populations grow very rapidly; this accelerating pattern of increasing population size is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Exponential Growth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Exponential growth refers to the rapid increase in population size when resources are unlimited, resulting in a J-shaped growth curve.
 
• This type of growth occurs when the birth rate significantly exceeds the death rate, leading to accelerated population expansion.
 
• Exponential growth is often observed in ideal conditions where there are no limiting factors such as food, space, or predation.
 
• It is mathematically modeled as P(t)=P0ert P(t) = P_0 e^{rt} , where P(t) P(t) is the population at time t t , P0 P_0 is the initial population, r r is the growth rate, and e e is Euler's number.
 
• While exponential growth can occur temporarily, it is unsustainable in the long term due to environmental limitations and competition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Logistic Growth:**

 
 
• Logistic growth occurs when population growth slows down and stabilizes as it approaches the carrying capacity.
 
• It is represented by an S-shaped curve and accounts for limiting factors like resources and space.
 
 
 
• **Carrying Capacity:**
 
 
• Carrying capacity is the maximum population size that an environment can sustain indefinitely without degradation.
 
• It is determined by the availability of resources, competition, and environmental conditions.
 
 
 
• **Population Explosion:**
 
 
• Refers to an extremely rapid increase in population size, typically due to high birth rates and reduced mortality rates.
 
• Population explosion can lead to resource depletion and environmental challenges.
 
 
 
• **Factors Influencing Population Growth:**
 
 
• Birth rate, death rate, immigration, and emigration are key factors impacting population growth.
 
• Environmental conditions, healthcare advancements, and socio-economic factors also play significant roles.

questions.question: In which position did India finish in the Para Asian Games event in 2023?

• China topped the medal tally, followed by Iran, Japan, and South Korea, with India emerging as a significant sporting nation in para sports.
 
• The 2023 Para Asian Games were held from **October 22 to October 28, 2023**, and saw participation from over 40 countries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The event promotes inclusivity and celebrates the achievements of para-athletes across Asia.
 
• The first edition of the Para Asian Games was held in Guangzhou, China, in 2010.
 
 
 
• **India's Growth in Para Sports**
 
 
• India has made significant progress in para sports, thanks to the efforts of organizations like the **Paralympic Committee of India**.
 
• Government initiatives such as the **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)** and increased funding have contributed to improved performances.

• Advanced facilities and high-tech arrangements in Hangzhou ensured a smooth and inclusive event for all participants.

questions.question: Which characteristic pottery became a hallmark of early Iron Age settlements in northern India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Painted Grey Ware**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Painted Grey Ware (PGW)** is a type of pottery that emerged as a hallmark of early Iron Age settlements in northern India, particularly during the Vedic period (circa 1200–600 BCE).
 
• This pottery is characterized by its fine texture, grey color, and painted designs in black or deep brown hues, often depicting geometric patterns or simple motifs.
 
• PGW is strongly associated with settlements located in the Indo-Gangetic plains, including sites like Hastinapur, Ahichchhatra, and Atranjikhera.
 
• Archaeological findings suggest that PGW pottery reflects the cultural and technological advancements during the early Iron Age, coinciding with the transition from pastoral to agrarian societies.
 
• It is often linked with the later Vedic culture and is considered one of the indicators of early urbanization in northern India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Black-and-Red Ware:**

 
 
• A type of pottery associated with Chalcolithic cultures and some Iron Age sites in India.
 
• It features a dual-color scheme with black interiors and red exteriors, often with simple decorations.
 
• While significant, it predates Painted Grey Ware and is not specific to early Iron Age settlements.
 
 
 
• **Northern Black Polished Ware (NBPW):**
 
 
• NBPW pottery is a later development, flourishing around 700–200 BCE during the Mauryan period.
 
• It is known for its glossy finish and was often associated with urban centers and trade networks.
 
 
 
• **Red Polished Ware:**
 
 
• This type of pottery is typically associated with later periods, such as the post-Mauryan and Gupta periods.
 
• It is characterized by its bright red color and smooth texture, often used for decorative purposes.
 
 
 
• **Early Iron Age Settlements:**
 
 
• The period saw the rise of agrarian societies, advancements in metallurgy, and the use of iron tools and weapons.
 
• Settlements like Hastinapur and Kaushambi flourished during this era, marking the transition to urbanization.

questions.question: How many five-year plans were covered during 1951-1990?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India implemented a total of **7 five-year plans** between 1951 and 1990.
 
• The first five-year plan began in **1951**, focusing on agricultural development and infrastructure.
 
• Subsequent plans aimed at industrialization, poverty reduction, and economic growth.
 
• The **seventh five-year plan (1985-1990)** emphasized productivity, modernization, and self-reliance.
 
• The planning process during this period was overseen by the **Planning Commission**, established in 1950.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans in India:**

 
 
• Introduced in 1951, inspired by the Soviet Union's model of centralized economic planning.
 
• Aimed to set targets for national development over a five-year period.
 
 
 
• **Planning Commission:**
 
 
• Established in 1950 by the Government of India.
 
• Responsible for formulating and overseeing five-year plans until its dissolution in 2014.
 
 
 
• **Major Focus Areas:**
 
 
• Agriculture (First Plan), Industrialization (Second Plan), Poverty Alleviation (Fourth Plan).
 
• Self-reliance and modernization (Seventh Plan).
 
 
 
• **Transition After 1990:**
 
 
• The era of economic liberalization started in 1991, shifting focus to market-driven reforms.
 
• Five-year plans continued until 2017, replaced by the **NITI Aayog** framework.

questions.question: Which of the following dancers won the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Chhau dance in 2018?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tapan Kumar Pattanayak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Tapan Kumar Pattanayak** is a renowned Indian dancer known for his expertise in Chhau dance, a traditional Indian dance form.
 
• He was awarded the prestigious **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** for Chhau dance in 2018, recognizing his contributions to this art form.
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award is India's highest honor for performing arts, given by the National Academy of Music, Dance, and Drama.
 
• Chhau dance has three main styles: **Seraikella Chhau, Purulia Chhau, and Mayurbhanj Chhau**, each originating from different regions of India.
 
• Tapan Kumar Pattanayak has played a vital role in preserving and promoting the Mayurbhanj Chhau style, which is characterized by its energetic movements and martial art elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chhau Dance**

 
 
• Chhau is a semi-classical Indian dance form that incorporates martial arts, folklore, and storytelling.
 
• It is primarily performed in the states of Odisha, Jharkhand, and West Bengal.
 
• Chhau dance uses masks in some styles, such as Purulia Chhau, whereas Mayurbhanj Chhau is performed without masks.
 
• The themes of Chhau performances often revolve around episodes from Hindu epics like the Ramayana and Mahabharata.
 
 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi**
 
 
• Established in 1952, Sangeet Natak Akademi is India's National Academy for Music, Dance, and Drama.
 
• The Akademi Awards are conferred annually to artists for their outstanding achievements in performing arts.
 
• It aims to preserve and promote India's rich cultural heritage and traditional art forms.
 
 
 
• **Mayurbhanj Chhau Dance**
 
 
• Originating from Odisha, Mayurbhanj Chhau is a mask-less version of Chhau dance.
 
• It is known for its vigorous and dynamic movements, often depicting themes of heroism and mythology.
 
• Mayurbhanj Chhau incorporates elements of acrobatics and martial arts, making it visually captivating.
 
 
 
• **Key Figures in Chhau Dance**
 
 
• Many notable artists have contributed to the development and preservation of Chhau dance, including **Tapan Kumar Pattanayak**.
 
• Efforts by dancers and cultural institutions have helped Chhau gain recognition both nationally and internationally.

questions.question: In which state is the Halda Festival celebrated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Himachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Halda Festival is a cultural celebration observed in the **Lahaul-Spiti district** of Himachal Pradesh.
 
• This festival is celebrated to honor the Hindu deity **Goddess Kali** and to seek blessings for prosperity and well-being.
 
• It is celebrated during the winter season, particularly in **January**, depending on the lunar calendar.
 
• The festival involves a traditional ritual where villagers light a bonfire using cedar branches, symbolizing unity and harmony.
 
• Halda is distinct for its communal participation, with villagers coming together to celebrate and strengthen social bonds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Himachal Pradesh**

 
 
• Known as the **"Land of Gods"**, Himachal Pradesh is famous for its rich cultural heritage and traditions.
 
• It is home to numerous festivals such as **Dussehra of Kullu**, **Losar Festival**, and **Minjar Fair**.
 
• The state is known for its scenic beauty, including the Himalayas, rivers, and valleys.
 
• Himachal Pradesh plays a vital role in preserving Indian tribal and folk traditions.
 
 
 
• **Lahaul-Spiti Region**
 
 
• Lahaul-Spiti is a tribal region in Himachal Pradesh known for its rugged terrain and Buddhist culture.
 
• The region experiences extreme winters, and festivals like Halda offer an opportunity for socializing.
 
• It is also famous for ancient monasteries such as **Key Monastery** and **Tabo Monastery**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Goddess Kali**
 
 
• Goddess Kali is a significant deity in Hinduism, symbolizing strength, protection, and the destruction of evil.
 
• She is often invoked during festivals for blessings and protection from adversities.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Festivals of India**
 
 
• India is known for its diversity of festivals, which reflect the cultural and religious plurality of the country.
 
• Festivals like Halda not only preserve traditions but also promote community bonding and cultural identity.

questions.question: According to the Census of India 2011, which of the following state has the least population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mizoram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Census of India 2011, **Mizoram** had the least population among the listed states.
 
• The total population of Mizoram in 2011 was approximately **1,091,014**, making it one of the least populated states in India.
 
• Mizoram is a northeastern state of India, known for its hilly terrain and dense forests.
 
• Among the northeastern states mentioned (Assam, Manipur, Tripura, and Mizoram), Mizoram had the lowest population figures as per the census.
 
• Despite its low population, Mizoram boasts a high literacy rate of about **91.33%** as per the 2011 Census.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census of India:**

 
 
• The Census is conducted every 10 years by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
• The Census of India 2011 was the 15th national census since the first census conducted in 1872.
 
• It provides comprehensive data on population, literacy, gender ratio, and other demographic factors.
 
 
 
• **Population Distribution in India:**
 
 
• India's population is unevenly distributed due to geographic, economic, and social factors.
 
• States like Uttar Pradesh have the highest population, whereas smaller states like Mizoram and Sikkim have much lower populations.
 
 
 
• **Mizoram:**
 
 
• Mizoram is one of the seven sister states in northeast India.
 
• The state is characterized by its tribal communities and unique cultural heritage.
 
• Mizoram's economy is primarily agrarian, with shifting cultivation being a common practice.
 
 
 
• **Literacy Rate:**
 
 
• The literacy rate is an important parameter measured during the Census.
 
• Mizoram's literacy rate of 91.33% (2011 Census) is one of the highest in India, showcasing its focus on education.

questions.question: In which year was the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan launched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2021**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan** was officially launched on **13th October 2021** by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
 
• This plan aims to provide **multimodal connectivity infrastructure** to various economic zones in the country.
 
• It focuses on **integrated infrastructure planning** and coordination among different government departments to improve logistics efficiency and reduce costs.
 
• The initiative is a part of the government’s strategy to make India a global manufacturing hub by streamlining **transport, supply chains, and infrastructure development**.
 
• It is aligned with the goal of achieving a **$5 trillion economy** by addressing critical bottlenecks in infrastructure development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Objectives of PM Gati Shakti:**

 
 
• Enhance coordination among departments to ensure integrated planning and implementation of infrastructure projects.
 
• Reduce logistics costs to make Indian businesses more competitive globally.
 
• Support India’s goal of becoming a global manufacturing and export hub.
 
 
 
• **Components of the Gati Shakti Plan:**
 
 
• Involves a **Geospatial Digital Platform** for real-time data monitoring and project tracking.
 
• Includes **16 ministries**, such as Railways, Roads and Highways, Power, and Telecom, working together for integrated infrastructure development.
 
 
 
• **National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP):**
 
 
• PM Gati Shakti is closely integrated with the **NIP**, which was launched in 2019.
 
• NIP aims to invest over **Rs. 111 lakh crore** in infrastructure by 2025 across sectors like energy, roads, railways, and urban development.
 
 
 
• **Multimodal Connectivity:**
 
 
• Focuses on connecting ports, airports, railways, and roadways to facilitate seamless movement of goods and services.
 
• Encourages the use of modern technologies, such as drones and GIS-based mapping, for better planning and execution.

questions.question: The oceanic crust is mostly made up of different types of basalt which extends how many kilometres beneath the ocean floor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5-10 km**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The oceanic crust is primarily composed of basalt, a dense, dark volcanic rock.
 
• The thickness of the oceanic crust ranges from **5 to 10 kilometers** beneath the ocean floor, depending on its age and location.
 
• New oceanic crust is formed at mid-ocean ridges due to volcanic activity and spreads outward over time.
 
• It is thinner and denser than the continental crust, which is mostly composed of granite and is around 30-50 km thick.
 
• The oceanic crust is a crucial part of the Earth's lithosphere and plays a significant role in the plate tectonic cycle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Basalt**

 
 
• Basalt is a volcanic igneous rock that makes up the majority of the oceanic crust.
 
• It is rich in minerals like pyroxene, plagioclase, and olivine, and has a high density compared to continental crust rocks.
 
 
 
• **Mid-Ocean Ridges**
 
 
• These are underwater mountain ranges where new oceanic crust is formed due to tectonic plate divergence.
 
• Examples include the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and the East Pacific Rise.
 
 
 
• **Plate Tectonics**
 
 
• The oceanic crust is part of the Earth's lithosphere, which is divided into tectonic plates.
 
• Plates interact at boundaries, leading to processes like subduction, where oceanic crust is pushed beneath continental crust, recycling it into the mantle.
 
 
 
• **Oceanic vs. Continental Crust**
 
 
• Oceanic crust is thinner (5-10 km) but denser, while continental crust is thicker (30-50 km) but less dense.
 
• The differences in composition and density play a key role in tectonic processes like subduction and mountain building.
 
 
 
• **Seafloor Spreading**
 
 
• The process by which new oceanic crust is created at mid-ocean ridges and spreads outward.
 
• This phenomenon provides evidence for the theory of plate tectonics, as observed through magnetic patterns on the seafloor.

questions.question: Which Directive Principle advocates the organisation of village panchayats for selfgovernment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 40**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 40 of the Indian Constitution directs the state to organize village panchayats and empower them to function as units of self-government.
 
• This provision is included under the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), which are non-justiciable guidelines for governance.
 
• The concept of village panchayats aligns with Mahatma Gandhi’s vision of decentralized governance and rural empowerment.
 
• Village panchayats play a significant role in local administration and decision-making, fostering grassroots democracy.
 
• Article 40 emphasizes the principle of decentralization to ensure efficient governance and equitable development in rural areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP):**

 
 
• DPSPs are enshrined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution (Articles 36-51).
 
• They are non-enforceable in courts but serve as guiding principles for governance aimed at achieving socio-economic justice.
 
 
 
• **Decentralized Governance:**
 
 
• Decentralization involves the distribution of decision-making powers to lower levels of government, such as village panchayats.
 
• This ensures better representation, accountability, and efficient resource utilization at the local level.
 
 
 
• **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act:**
 
 
• This act, passed in 1992, established the Panchayati Raj system in India.
 
• It provided constitutional status to village panchayats and detailed their powers, composition, and functions.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Village Panchayats:**
 
 
• Village panchayats serve as the foundation of rural development and local self-governance.
 
• They handle essential functions like sanitation, water supply, education, and rural infrastructure development.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the new Chairperson of the Union Public Service Commission on 1 August 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Preeti Sudan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Preeti Sudan** was appointed as the Chairperson of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) on **1 August 2024**.
 
• She succeeded Dr. Manoj Soni, the former Chairperson of UPSC.
 
• Preeti Sudan is a retired Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer from the **1983 batch of the Andhra Pradesh cadre**.
 
• She has served as the **Union Health Secretary** and played a key role in shaping policies during the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• Her experience in various administrative roles makes her highly qualified for heading UPSC, the premier recruiting agency for the Indian government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC):**

 
 
• UPSC is a constitutional body established under **Article 315** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It conducts prestigious exams like the Civil Services Examination, Engineering Services Examination, and others.
 
• UPSC is responsible for recruiting candidates for top administrative positions in the Indian government.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Chairperson of UPSC:**
 
 
• The Chairperson leads the commission in conducting examinations and interviews for government recruitment.
 
• They ensure transparency, fairness, and integrity in the recruitment process.
 
 
 
• **Preeti Sudan’s Career Highlights:**
 
 
• She played a crucial role in the implementation of **Ayushman Bharat**, India’s flagship health insurance scheme.
 
• She also contributed to the drafting of the National Health Policy 2017.
 
• Her administrative experience spans sectors like education, finance, and health.
 
 
 
• **Importance of UPSC Chairperson:**
 
 
• The Chairperson’s leadership influences the quality of governance through the selection of top-tier officials.
 
• They uphold the constitutional mandate of impartiality and merit-based selection in public service recruitment.

questions.question: How many priorities were adopted in the Union Budget for the financial year 2023-24?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Union Budget 2023-24 adopted **seven priorities**, referred to as the "Saptarishi" to guide India's Amrit Kaal journey.
 
• The seven priorities are **Inclusive Development, Reaching the Last Mile, Infrastructure and Investment, Unleashing Potential, Green Growth, Youth Power, and Financial Sector.**
 
• Each priority is aligned with the vision of fostering sustainable economic growth and achieving India's long-term development goals.
 
• These priorities reflect the government's commitment to inclusivity, innovation, and environmental sustainability in policymaking.
 
• The Union Budget 2023-24 was presented by **Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman** on February 1, 2023.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Amrit Kaal:**

 
 
• A term introduced by the government to define the 25-year period leading up to India’s centenary of independence in 2047.
 
• It emphasizes India's vision for inclusive and sustainable development during this transformative era.
 
 
 
• **Green Growth:**
 
 
• One of the seven priorities aimed at promoting sustainable practices and reducing carbon emissions.
 
• Includes initiatives like green hydrogen, energy transition, and renewable energy expansion.
 
 
 
• **Reaching the Last Mile:**
 
 
• Focuses on ensuring that the benefits of government schemes and initiatives reach the underserved and marginalized sections of society.
 
• Includes targeted development for tribal regions and vulnerable groups.
 
 
 
• **Infrastructure and Investment:**
 
 
• Aims at enhancing capital investment to boost economic growth and job creation.
 
• Proposes an increased capital expenditure of ₹10 lakh crore for the fiscal year 2023-24.

questions.question: Which of the following sectors was given the highest priority in the First Five-Year Plan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Agriculture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The First Five-Year Plan (1951–1956) of India focused primarily on **agriculture and irrigation** as its highest priority.
 
• This emphasis was due to the significant challenges of food shortages and the need for self-sufficiency in food production post-independence.
 
• Agriculture accounted for approximately **31% of the total plan allocation**, highlighting its critical importance.
 
• The plan aimed to improve agricultural productivity through **land reforms, community development programs, and irrigation projects**.
 
• Key initiatives included major irrigation projects like the Bhakra Nangal Dam to enhance water resources for farming.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans of India:**

 
 
• India adopted the five-year plan model from the Soviet Union to achieve planned economic development.
 
• The Planning Commission, established in 1950, was responsible for formulating and implementing these plans.
 
• The First Five-Year Plan focused on **agriculture, irrigation, and energy production** to address immediate needs.
 
 
 
• **Land Reforms:**
 
 
• Land reforms under the First Five-Year Plan aimed to abolish the zamindari system and redistribute land to farmers.
 
• These reforms included tenancy rights, land ceilings, and consolidation of land holdings.
 
 
 
• **Community Development Program (1952):**
 
 
• This program was launched to promote rural development through agriculture, education, health, and infrastructure.
 
• It served as a model for integrated rural development during the First Five-Year Plan.
 
 
 
• **Major Irrigation Projects:**
 
 
• Projects like Bhakra Nangal Dam, Hirakud Dam, and Damodar Valley Corporation were initiated to address water scarcity and improve agricultural irrigation.
 
• These projects played a vital role in enhancing agricultural productivity in India.
 
 
 
• **Economic Growth Target:**
 
 
• The First Five-Year Plan aimed at an annual growth rate of 2.1% but achieved a higher growth rate of 3.6% due to agricultural success.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT considered a state executive?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chief Justice of High Court**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Chief Justice of a High Court is part of the **judiciary** and not the state executive, which primarily consists of political and administrative heads.
 
• The state executive comprises the **Governor, Chief Minister, and the Council of Ministers**, all of whom are responsible for the administration and governance of the state.
 
• The Chief Justice and judges of the High Court are responsible for interpreting laws and ensuring justice, which falls under the jurisdiction of the judiciary and not the executive branch.
 
• The **separation of powers** doctrine clearly distinguishes the judiciary from the executive to maintain checks and balances in governance.
 
• While the Governor appoints the Chief Minister and other ministers, the judiciary remains independent and is governed by the provisions of the Constitution of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Governor:**

 
 
• The Governor is the constitutional head of a state and is appointed by the President of India for a term of five years.
 
• They act as the representative of the Union Government in the state.
 
• The Governor has executive, legislative, and discretionary powers, including appointing the Chief Minister and dissolving the State Assembly.
 
 
 
• **Chief Minister:**
 
 
• The Chief Minister is the real executive head of a state and is responsible for formulating policies and governance within the state.
 
• They are appointed by the Governor, usually the leader of the majority party in the state legislature.
 
 
 
• **Council of Ministers:**
 
 
• The Council of Ministers, headed by the Chief Minister, aids and advises the Governor in the administration of the state.
 
• They are collectively responsible to the State Legislature.
 
 
 
• **Judiciary:**
 
 
• The High Court is the highest judicial authority in a state and functions independently of the executive and legislature.
 
• The Chief Justice of the High Court is appointed by the President of India in consultation with the Chief Justice of India and the Governor of the state.
 
• The judiciary ensures adherence to the Constitution and protects the fundamental rights of citizens.

questions.question: Which group was formed in 1919 to support the Khilafat Movement and strengthen the Hindu-Muslim unity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Khilafat Committee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Khilafat Committee was established in 1919 to protest against the injustices meted out to the Ottoman Caliphate after World War I and to protect its authority.
 
• It aimed to support the Khilafat Movement and foster Hindu-Muslim unity in the Indian independence struggle.
 
• The leaders of the Khilafat Movement included prominent figures like Maulana Mohammad Ali and Maulana Shaukat Ali, also known as the Ali Brothers.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi supported the Khilafat Movement, encouraging Indian Muslims and Hindus to work together against British colonial rule.
 
• The movement eventually merged with the Non-Cooperation Movement initiated by Gandhi, forming a united front against British oppression.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khilafat Movement:**

 
 
• The movement was a pan-Islamic political campaign launched by Indian Muslims to influence the British government and protect the Ottoman Caliphate after World War I.
 
• The Treaty of Sèvres (1920), which dismantled the Ottoman Empire, was a major catalyst for this movement.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Ali Brothers:**
 
 
• Maulana Mohammad Ali and Maulana Shaukat Ali were instrumental in leading the Khilafat Movement in India.
 
• They worked in collaboration with Mahatma Gandhi to ensure Hindu-Muslim unity during the struggle for independence.
 
 
 
• **Hindu-Muslim Unity:**
 
 
• The Khilafat Movement marked a rare period of collaboration between Hindus and Muslims in the Indian freedom struggle.
 
• Gandhi's support for the movement was pivotal in bridging communal gaps temporarily.
 
 
 
• **Decline of the Movement:**
 
 
• The Khilafat Movement declined after Mustafa Kemal Atatürk abolished the Caliphate in 1924 and established a secular government in Turkey.
 
• This development weakened the relevance of the movement in India.

questions.question: Jagjit Singh was associated with which of the following fields of music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ghazal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jagjit Singh was popularly known as the **“Ghazal King”** for his contributions to the Indian music industry, particularly in the genre of Ghazals.
 
• He is credited with making **Ghazals more accessible to the masses** by blending traditional Ghazal music with modern instrumentation.
 
• Jagjit Singh’s albums such as **“The Unforgettable,” “Mirage,” and “Hope”** are iconic works in the Ghazal genre.
 
• He performed in multiple languages including Hindi, Punjabi, and Urdu, showcasing his versatility as a Ghazal singer and composer.
 
• His contribution to Ghazal music earned him several awards, including the **Sahitya Kala Academy Award** and recognition as a pivotal figure in Indian music history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ghazal:**

 
 
• Ghazal is a poetic form consisting of rhyming couplets and a refrain, with each line sharing the same meter.
 
• Originating in Arabic literature, Ghazals later became popular in Persian, Urdu, and Indian literature and music.
 
• It often expresses themes of love, loss, and mysticism, making it a highly emotive form of art.
 
 
 
• **Jagjit Singh’s Legacy:**
 
 
• He was the first Indian musician to record a digital album.
 
• His music played a significant role in **reviving the Ghazal genre** during the late 20th century.
 
• Jagjit Singh collaborated with prominent poets like **Kaifi Azmi and Gulzar** to bring poetry to life through his music.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Indian Music:**
 
 
• Jagjit Singh’s work bridged the gap between classical music and contemporary tastes.
 
• He introduced **simple, relatable lyrics** in Ghazals, making the genre widely appreciated by diverse audiences.

questions.question: Which of the following is a correct balanced chemical equation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1: 2C4H10(l) + 13O2(g) → 8CO2(g) + 10H2O**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The chemical equation **2C4H10(l) + 13O2(g) → 8CO2(g) + 10H2O** represents the complete combustion of butane (C4H10).
 
• In a balanced chemical equation, the number of atoms of each element on the reactant side must equal those on the product side.
 
• Here, 2 molecules of butane react with 13 molecules of oxygen to produce 8 molecules of carbon dioxide and 10 molecules of water.
 
• The balancing ensures that **carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen atoms** are conserved during the reaction according to the law of conservation of mass.
 
• This equation is commonly used in the study of hydrocarbon combustion reactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Combustion Reaction**

 
 
• A combustion reaction occurs when a hydrocarbon reacts with oxygen to produce carbon dioxide, water, and energy.
 
• Complete combustion happens when there is enough oxygen available, producing CO2 and H2O as the only products.
 
 
 
• **Law of Conservation of Mass**
 
 
• This law states that matter cannot be created or destroyed in a chemical reaction.
 
• In a balanced equation, the mass and number of atoms on the reactant side must equal the mass and number of atoms on the product side.
 
 
 
• **Hydrocarbons**
 
 
• Hydrocarbons are organic compounds consisting entirely of carbon and hydrogen.
 
• They are categorized into alkanes, alkenes, and alkynes based on the type of bonds between carbon atoms.
 
• Butane (C4H10) is an alkane, characterized by single bonds between carbon atoms.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Combustion Reactions**
 
 
• Combustion reactions are crucial for energy production in industries, vehicles, and households.
 
• Fuels like propane, butane, and methane undergo combustion to generate heat and power.

questions.question: Which of the following teams did Tamil Nadu defeat in the final to win the men's title in he 71st$ Senior National Basketball Championship 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Tamil Nadu defeated Punjab in the final match to secure the men's title in the **71st Senior National Basketball Championship 2022**.
 
• The final game took place at **Chennai, Tamil Nadu**, where the championship was hosted.
 
• Tamil Nadu showcased exceptional performance, winning the men's title with a scoreline of **87-69** against Punjab.
 
• The victory highlighted Tamil Nadu's dominance in the basketball circuit in India.
 
• This championship is one of the prestigious national-level tournaments in basketball, organized under the aegis of the **Basketball Federation of India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Basketball Federation of India (BFI):**

 
 
• The BFI is the governing body for basketball in India and is responsible for organizing national-level tournaments like the Senior National Basketball Championship.
 
• Founded in 1950, it works to promote basketball across the country and represents India in international basketball events.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Senior National Basketball Championship:**
 
 
• This championship provides a platform for players from different states to showcase their talent and compete at the highest level in India.
 
• It is considered a crucial event for the selection of players for the national basketball team.
 
 
 
• **Basketball in India:**
 
 
• Basketball has been growing steadily in popularity, especially among youth, due to increased exposure to international leagues like the NBA.
 
• India has been making efforts to improve infrastructure and coaching standards to develop basketball at grassroots levels.
 
 
 
• **Tamil Nadu's Basketball Legacy:**
 
 
• Tamil Nadu has traditionally been one of the strongholds in Indian basketball, consistently performing well in national championships.
 
• The state has produced several talented players who have represented India at international levels.
